title: Take VAT off domestic gas as well as electricity
headline: Gas to 0%, as electricity already is. Costs about £0.8bn a year.
description: Domestic fuel and power pay the 5% reduced rate; the government took electricity to 0% from 1 October 2026 and said that costs about £850 million in 2026-27, a half year. This card takes gas and the other domestic fuels to 0% as well. HMRC costs the whole 5% relief against 20% at £7.0bn in 2025-26, so the last five points on all domestic fuel and power are a third of that; taking off the electricity part, at twice the government's half-year figure, leaves £633 million in 2025-26, grown with the OBR's VAT forecast: about £0.8bn a year.

baselinePolicy.text: Domestic fuel and power pay the 5% reduced rate in the March 2026 baseline; electricity was cut to 0% from 1 October 2026, after the forecast, at a cost the government put at about £850 million in 2026-27.
alreadyIncludes: The 5% reduced rate on domestic fuel and power, costed by HMRC at £7.0bn in 2025-26 against the 20% standard rate (Estimated cost of tax reliefs, Table 2, row VAT NS4).

terms.label: HMRC's cost of the 5% rate on all domestic fuel and power against 20%; the last five points are a third of the fifteen

source.note: row vat-ns4, Domestic fuel and power

terms.label: Less the electricity cut already made: the government's half-year figure for 2026-27, doubled to a full year

rawSource.note: Static arithmetic. A third of HMRC's relief cost is what the last five points on all domestic fuel and power are worth; the electricity share is removed at twice the government's stated half-year cost, because the Treasury has published no full-year figure yet. The remainder is gas and other fuels, grown with the OBR's VAT receipts from 2025-26.

caveats: Annualising the £850 million is ours: the government's figure is for the six months from 1 October 2026 and the Treasury promised a full-year costing at the Budget. If the true full-year electricity cost differs, this figure moves pound for pound the other way.
Static: cheaper gas means a little more gas used, and HMRC's relief figures carry no behavioural response. The 2025-26 relief cost is HMRC's projection, not an outturn.
Gas, heating oil, coal and other domestic fuels are treated together, because HMRC costs the relief as one line.

considerations.text: The figure is the cost of the last five points at today's spending. A lower price means slightly more gas bought, so the true cost would be a little higher; HMRC's relief estimates do not model such responses.

Every household on mains gas gains, by more the more they burn; the government said the electricity cut took about £45 a year off a price-cap bill. Homes heated by electricity, heat pumps or district heating gain nothing from this one, and the relief is worth most to large, old, gas-heated homes.

interactions.text: They pull opposite ways: this takes gas to 0%, that takes all domestic fuel and power to 20%. Switch on one or the other.
The reduced rate lever changes the 5% that gas pays; this lever takes gas out of the reduced rate altogether, so the two overlap.
